previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A 65-year-old man with a history of primary central nervous system B-cell lymphoma was admitted for his 28th cycle of high-dose methotrexate chemotherapy, along with rituximab and temozolomide. He reported recent dysuria, and a urine culture grew Group B streptococcus, leading to a course of cefdinir. Admission sodium was low at 130, attributed to excessive desmopressin use for urinary frequency; the medication was held initially and restarted at a reduced dose once sodium stabilized. Methotrexate was administered without complications, with appropriate leucovorin rescue and bicarbonate hydration. His CNS lymphoma remains in remission per recent imaging, and he had no seizure activity during admission. He was discharged home in stable condition with instructions to complete oral leucovorin and sodium bicarbonate, finish antibiotics, and continue temozolomide on a 7-days-on, 7-days-off schedule, with oncology follow-up planned in two to three months.

EXAMINATION:  LIVER OR GALLBLADDER US (SINGLE ORGAN) PORT

INDICATION:  ___ year old man with CNS lymphoma on methotrexate, also alcohol
use, has RUQ tenderness  // eval for gallstones, hepatomegaly

TECHNIQUE:  Grey scale and color Doppler ultrasound images of the abdomen were
obtained.

COMPARISON:  CT abdomen and pelvis, ___.

FINDINGS: 

LIVER: The liver is diffusely echogenic, but no focal lesion is seen. There is
no focal liver mass. Main portal vein is patent with hepatopetal flow. There
is no ascites.

BILE DUCTS: There is no intrahepatic biliary dilation. The CBD measures 5 mm.

GALLBLADDER: There is no evidence of stones or gallbladder wall thickening.

PANCREAS: The pancreas is not well visualized, likely due to overlying bowel
gas.

SPLEEN: Normal echogenicity, measuring 12.2 cm.

IMPRESSION: 

1.  Echogenic liver compatible with hepatic steatosis, though other forms of
chronic liver disease including significant hepatic fibrosis/cirrhosis cannot
be excluded.
2.  No cholelithiasis.

INDICATION:  ___ year old man with CNS lymphoma receiving MTX// please do flow
study and catheter stripping

COMPARISON:  Chest radiograph from ___

TECHNIQUE:   OPERATORS: Dr. ___ resident) and Dr. ___
___ radiology attending) performed the procedure. The attending,
Dr. ___ was present and supervising throughout the procedure. Dr. ___,
___ radiologist, personally supervised the trainee during the key
components of the procedure and reviewed and agreed with the trainee's
findings.
ANESTHESIA: Moderate sedation was provided by administrating divided doses of
50mcg of fentanyl and 1 mg of midazolam throughout the total intra-service
time of 50 mins during which the patient's hemodynamic parameters were
continuously monitored by an independent trained radiology nurse. 1% lidocaine
was injected in the skin and subcutaneous tissues overlying the access site.
MEDICATIONS: 1% local lidocaine
CONTRAST: 40 ml of Optiray contrast.
FLUOROSCOPY TIME AND DOSE: 14.43 m, 7266 cGy-cm2

PROCEDURE:  1. Right common femoral venous access using ultrasound.
2. DSA venogram through both ports of the tunneled line using a hand
injection.
3. Catheter stripping performed through a right common femoral vein approach
using an Ensnare endovascular snare.
4. Post-stripping DSA venogram through the  port using a hand injection.

PROCEDURE DETAILS:
Following the explanation of the risks, benefits and alternatives to the
procedure, written informed consent was obtained from the patient/from the
healthcare proxy/using an interpreter. The patient was then brought to the
angiography suite and placed supine on the exam table. A pre-procedure
time-out was performed per ___ protocol. The right groin was prepped and
draped in the usual sterile fashion.

Both hubs of the port were sequentially injected with contrast and a DSA
venogram was performed. Under continuous ultrasound guidance, the patent right
common femoral vein was compressible and accessed using a micropuncture
needle. Permanent ultrasound images were obtained before and after intravenous
access, which confirmed vein patency. Subsequently, a Nitinol wire was passed
into the IVC using fluoroscopic guidance. A small incision was made at the
needle entry site. The needle was exchanged for a micropuncture sheath. The
Nitinol wire was removed and ___ wire was advanced distally into the
IVC. The micropuncture sheath was removed and a 55 cm 7 ___ sheath was
advanced over the wire and the inner dilator was removed. The sheath was
flushed with saline and then a 9-15mm Ensnare device was advanced through the
sheath up to the tunneled catheter tip.

Multiple stripping were performed using the snare. Following successful
stripping, contrast was injected through the catheter and a DSA venogram was
performed and the ports flushed and aspirated.

The wire, catheters and sheath were then removed from the right groin and
manual pressure was used to achieve hemostasis. Sterile dressings were
applied. The patient tolerated the procedure well and there were no immediate
post-procedure complications.

FINDINGS: 

1. The accessed vein was patent and compressible.
2. Pre-stripping venogram showing a fibrin sheath and retrograde flow
3. Post-stripping venogram showing much improved appropriate forward flow into
the SVC.
4. Examination of the snare showed extensive removed fibrinous tissue

IMPRESSION: 

Successful stripping of a left sided port with blood return from both lumens.
The catheter is ready to use.
